Subject: Staggered commitment runway & escrow conditions for MSA/DPA/order form

Alex — great discussion on Friday. Per our mutual action plan, we want to propose a staggered commitment (pilot -> reserved capacity month 1 -> 12-month ramp) that aligns with your procurement windows. High level ask from Crestline we heard: evidence windows for SOC2/retention; escrow/escrow-trigger language; and a narrowly scoped DPA to cover PHI adjacency.

Draft suggestion from our side:
- Week 0–4: Pilot (trial usage, trial SLA) — no long-term commitment.
- Month 2–3: Transition to 3-month reserved capacity (discounted) contingent on acceptance criteria A/B.
- Month 4+: 12-month committed capacity (standard MSA + order form).

We can gate each step on acceptance criteria (test harness, evaluation MAP, and a signed order form). To keep legal throughput smooth, can your procurement accept a staged signature approach (Order form for pilot + separate signature for the MSA+DPA once redlines reconcile)? That lets you start ingesting data while legal finalizes the DPA.

I’m copying Karthik (pricing) and Marissa (CS handoff) — Laura from Legal will loop in for redlines if this approach is OK. I’ll attach an initial order form template and a one-pager DPA scope for your legal team to review.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks, this looks promising. A few clarifying questions from Procurement/Legal: 
1) Escrow trigger: Crestline needs an escrow that is only triggered on bankruptcy or extended inability to serve (>30 days). Can you confirm Redwood is OK with a narrowly scoped escrow (models + last 30 days of data) and that trigger language will be limited to insolvency/force majeure exhaustion?
2) DPA scope: our counsel asked for explicit sub-processor disclosure and a 30-day notification window for onboarding new subprocessors. Is that acceptable?
3) Acceptance criteria: can we formalize the A/B tests and define exact pass thresholds (latency P95 < 350ms, 1000 concurrent tokens/day for test)?

If we can get a redline by next Wed (7/7), procurement can fast-track approval and route signatures in the same week. Tim from procurement also asked if a phased discount could be added into the order form for committed months 4–15.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I’ll get our legal contact to send a redline if needed.

Best,
Alex
Director of Platform Engineering — Crestline Therapeutics

- DPA: explicit sub-processor notice window (30 days) and limited liability carve-outs around ingestion of PHI-adjacent data.

- DPA: accept 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors; include a registry URL (we’ll keep list updated). Add a clause for data segmentation and responsibilities around PHI-adjacent processing (we’ll limit liability where Redwood is not the processor of record).
- Order form: we’ll allow a phased discount schedule; pricing team to finalize numbers.

Also confirm whether Crestline will accept two-document signing (pilot order form now, MSA+DPA shortly after) versus a single-package signature.

I’ll upload redline to the shared drive and send a DocuSign-ready version once resolved. Targeting EOD Wed 7/7 but might be early if legal and pricing sync today.
